source_refs.note: Topic 16.2.2 with Figure 16.2 (pictograms), printed page 338. The pictograms themselves are not reproduced.

blocks.text: A laboratory worker must use chemicals according to the standard procedures, keeping in view the particular hazards and the precautions required for their safe use. Figure 16.2 shows the pictograms of chemical hazards.

blocks.alt: Nine red-bordered diamond pictograms with simple black symbols: explosive (a bursting bomb), flammable (a flame), oxidising (a flame over a circle), compressed gas (a gas cylinder), corrosive (liquid dripping from tubes onto a surface and a hand), toxic (a skull and crossbones), irritant or harmful (an exclamation mark), harmful to the environment (a dead tree and fish) and health hazard (a person with a star-shaped mark on the chest).
blocks.caption: Pictograms of chemical hazards (original diagram after Figure 16.2).
